version.title: Heat tolerance varies widely across wild _Saccharomyces_ isolates
version.subtitle: We measured growth across a temperature gradient for 84 wild _S. cerevisiae_ strains and found that thermotolerance correlates with the latitude of the strain’s collection site.
version.abstract:
Wild _Saccharomyces_ isolates show striking variation in tolerance to environmental stress, but the extent of variation across natural populations is poorly characterized. We collected 84 strains spanning a latitudinal range from the tropics to the boreal zone and measured growth rates across nine temperatures spanning 12–42 °C.

We found that thermotolerance was strongly correlated with the latitude of the collection site, with tropical strains showing the highest growth rates at temperatures above 37 °C and boreal strains growing best below 20 °C. The data point to local adaptation as the dominant driver of growth-temperature variation in this clade.
